description: SECURITY DEFENSE-IN-DEPTH: pin MIME header injection blocking via CR/LF \u2192 RFC2047 base64 (Subject) + extractName regex fail (From display-name). 2 new tests defend Bcc-injection regression class. test_count 400\u2192402, assertions/test 4.25\u21924.34.

asi.caught_class_of_bugs: MIME header injection via CR/LF in Subject or From display-name. Pre-pin: only the printable-ASCII regex (which excludes CR=0x0D and LF=0x0A) prevented injection — a regression that 'optimized' the regex to match Unicode control chars (e.g. /^[\u0020-\u007E]*$/u with /s flag, or replaced with /^[\x00-\x7F]*$/) would silently re-enable Bcc-injection attacks. Now pinned: (a) Subject containing \r\nBcc: triggers base64 wrap, no Bcc on wire; (b) From display-name containing CR/LF causes extractName regex to fail — display-name dropped, bare-email From only.

description: SECURITY FIX: webhook token compare \u2192 constant-time (OWASP ASVS V6.2.4 / NIST SP 800-63B). XOR-fold comparator with length-diff folded in first. 3 behavioral pins (length-mismatch / prefix-of-token / suffix-extended) catch buggy comparators. test_count 403\u2192404, branch_cov 98.05\u219298.07, assertions/test 4.33\u21924.34.

asi.caught_class_of_bugs: Webhook bearer-token timing attack: pre-fix `project.webhook_token !== token` exits on first mismatched byte, leaking secret bytes via response-time differences. While exploitability against a 48-char nanoid token over noisy CF Workers network is low, OWASP ASVS V6.2.4 / NIST SP 800-63B mandate constant-time compare for ALL secret/token equality checks. Standard secure-coding default. Implementation: XOR every byte into accumulator, walk MAX(a.length, b.length) iterations, fold length-diff into accumulator first so loop count is independent of the secret. Tests pin behavioral correctness on edge cases (length mismatch, prefix-of-token, suffix-extended) that catch the most common buggy comparators (loop-only-min-length — would falsely match prefix-of-token).
